About.title: About
About.intro: ALIN — African Legal Innovation Network is a pan-African legal innovation network born from a twofold observation:
About.point1: artificial intelligence is profoundly reshaping the skills and business models of legal professionals;
About.point2: and French-speaking Africa remains on the margins of the spaces where these transformations are debated and regulated.
About.body: Founded by Félicia Ombanda Indoumou, a CEMAC-accredited legal and tax adviser with over 13 years of experience in OHADA business law and tax advisory, ALIN is the network dedicated to legal and technological innovation in the French-speaking space — so that African jurists do not merely endure the changes driven by the rise of artificial intelligence, but take an active part in them.

Resources.title: Demystifying AI and law,
Resources.lede: Accessible content on AI and the law, focused on the practical issues for citizens and businesses.

items.title: AI and legal liability
items.text: Understand who is responsible when an AI system gets it wrong, and how to document decisions.

items.title: Personal data protection
items.text: Good practices for processing data in line with the legal framework and limiting non-compliance risks.

items.title: Automation and labour law
items.text: Potential impacts of AI on jobs, monitoring of employees and the employer's obligations.

items.title: Digital contracts
items.text: Essential clauses to secure a digital service, a software licence or an AI use case.

items.title: Evidence and traceability
items.text: How to preserve probative records in a digital environment (emails, logs, versions, signatures).

items.title: Operational compliance
items.text: Set up a simple foundation: internal policies, registers, minimal governance and periodic review.
